claims.scope: Exact TIM12 full RM chapter and bounded shared SDK lifecycle; no DMA capability.

contracts.detail: TIM12 is one 16-bit upcounter with two channels, one shared PSC/ARR/CCMR1, slave/master control and IRQ58. Base0x40001800, APB1L enable/reset/sleep/debug bit6. No down/center counting, encoder, ETR/external-clock2, DMA request/burst, break/complementary output, repetition counter, OCREF clear or TRGO2 is admitted. Family TIM_TypeDef fields are not instance capabilities. DS20 table6 merged general-purpose DMA-generation cell says Yes, while the exact header excludes TIM12 DMA and the exact RM DIER/register map has no DMA request/burst fields. This source conflict does not admit DMA; absence of a routing selector alone is not a hardware capability proof.

Ordinary timer kernel clock is HCLK under exact RCC configuration; getter is configured frequency, not a measurement. RM requires synchronous kernel/PCLK integer ratio1..16 and TI1/TI2/ITR inputs below kernel/4. Own producer readiness and selected remap; enable destination clock before triggers and do not change its clock while receiving them. Preserve DS external-clock ceiling discrepancy.

PSC divides by raw+1 (1..65536), buffered until UEV. ARR preload follows ARPE; zero ARR blocks counting. UDIS blocks UEV/shadow updates but UG still clears counter/prescaler. URS restricts update interrupt, not all update effects. UG can propagate TRGO. Nominal unsuppressed internal-clock steady overflow is kernel/((PSC+1)*(ARR+1)); trigger resets, OPM and dithering require separate timing.

CCxS changes require CCxE0. CCR read consumes CCxIF; repeated capture while flag set raises CCxOF. Read capture before testing overcapture. Capture prescaler1/2/4/8 resets when channel disabled and does not prescale trigger input. PWM input uses both channels, opposite polarity and shared slave reset.

Only OCM0..9,12,13 are described;10,11,14,15 reserved. PWM1/2 preloads and initial UG need explicit configuration. Combined PWM1/2 consumes both references with opposite PWM modes and OR/AND. Forced output still compares and raises flags. CCxE0 disables timer drive but GPIO/board state determines actual pad level. Output CCxNP must be0.

DITHEN modifies only with CEN0. ARR/CCR then use bits19:4 integer and3:0 fractional, raw maximum0xFFFEF. In normal mode upper bits19:16 reset. Fractional increments distribute across16 periods; capture low4 bits zero and CNT only integer. To disable: CEN0 and ARPE0, DITHEN0, clear CCIF, then restart. Average resolution is not individual-period timing.

Ordinary OPM stops CEN at next UEV and needs initial CNT<CCR<=ARR with CCR nonzero. Fast enable acts only PWM1/2. Retriggerable OPM uses SMS8 and OCM8/9 with CCR0 for this upcounter; each new trigger extends pulse. Generic down/center clauses are excluded. Hardware CEN stop does not establish software idle.

SMS valid0,4,5,6,7,8,9. Change TS only when unused, e.g. SMS0. Gated modes forbid TI1 edge-detector pulse. Trigger mode may set CEN by hardware; gated/external-clock1 needs software CEN. XOR combines TI1/TI2 with shared pre/post-filter placement and inversion, not extra channels.

ADSYNC requires same-source integer timer/ADC clock ratio and period or compare alignment. Enable ADC clock, configure timer/ADSYNC, enable ADC trigger reception, then start timer. Do not alter during operation. Setting a bit or selecting TRGO does not prove ADC route/readiness or jitter-free timing.

IRQ58 combines update/CC1/CC2/trigger. Flags are one-bit history; UIOVRF/CCxOF need loss accounting. Writes are16/32-bit; reads8/16/32-bit per RM1314. UIFREMAP copies UIF to CNT31. Sleep activity also needs RCC sleep gating; Stop stops and retains state, Standby requires reinit. Debug freeze requires HALTED1 and owned bit.

ES revision2 summary has no dedicated TIM12 entry; this is not absence of all composed errata. ES2.4.1 forbids simultaneous COMP1/COMP2 operation on revisionZ, relevant to TI remaps; Y marks that specific limitation not applicable. PC14/PC15 timer routes share oscillator pins: hash-bound board descriptor lists OSC32_IN net93 through R1/SB1 and OSC32_OUT net92 through R2/SB2. These are literal same-net memberships only; actual population/conduction and LSE ownership remain unverified. Apply ES2.2.x LSE restrictions whenever LSE is used and arbitrate oscillator versus timer-pin use.

source_derived_SDK_gates.detail: Generic APIs remain visible but exact header excludes TIM12 from DMA/burst/encoder/ETR/counter-mode predicates. These are largely assertion guards; release misuse can access reserved fields. SetConfig correctly skips counter-mode and repetition writes for TIM12, but dedicated counter-mode setter relies on assertion. Enforce exact capability admission before any API.

General period and OC pulse guards accept up to0xFFFEF independent of actual DITHEN; normal mode only16 bits, so acceptance does not preserve requested count. Generic OC mode validator accepts modes reserved on TIM12, including asymmetric modes and combined3/4. Restrict exact OCM domain and actual dithering representation even with debug assertions enabled. SDK OCM is5 bits: LL writes mask0x00030070 and shifted CH2 mask, including bit17/25 reserved on TIM12. Validate full raw code before truncation; combinedPWM3 raw16 would alias frozen0 if only low4 checked, asymmetricPWM9 raw24 would alias OPM8. Require bit4 zero.

Init is not a hardware reset. SetConfig changes selected fields and emits UG with temporary URS, without clearing UDIS/OPM/MMS or disabling channels; it resets software channel states. Channel Start/Stop controls CCxE independently from global CEN. Global idle is not proof all channels or pending events are quiescent. The reverse mismatch also occurs: configuring SMS6/8 while IDLE allows a hardware trigger to set CEN. Stop clears CEN but leaves SMS armed, so a later trigger can restart hardware while software remains IDLE. IDLE-only checks in dithering, ADSYNC and channel configuration do not prove CEN0. Quiesce trigger producers and verify actual counter state before restricted writes.

Compare/capture-unit configuration relies on global IDLE and does not disable CCxE before CCxS changes. OC polarity changes CCxP without clearing old IC CCxNP. Enforce channel-off and output NP0 before conversion. IC channel config alone does not configure CCxS; capture-unit setup is also required. CCxS3 captures from TRC only with an internal trigger selected; SetConfigCaptureUnit does not validate the current TS selection.

CC handler snapshots SR/DIER and clears flag before callback rather than reading CCR first; a new capture can overwrite data in that gap and callback read can clear the new flag. It does not account for CCxOF; generic update ignores UIOVRF. Dedicated update handler checks UIE without UIF. Pending-event/drain policy is required; no lossless callback guarantee.

HAL remap preserves unrelated selectors with unserialized RMW; LL source setter replaces all selector fields. Slave helper writes SMS before TS without neutralizing trigger first. Dither and ADC-sync helpers do not implement full RM sequencing or consumer readiness. Handle assertions do not serialize alternate handles or interrupts.

HAL_SetTriggerOutput asserts master capability but uses a family validator accepting OC3/OC4 raw6/7 and encoder clock raw8. LL writes full MMS mask including bit25 reserved on TIM12. Only raw0..5 are supported; debug assertions do not enforce this instance-specific domain.

conflicts.detail: RM1291 clock diagram includes ETR/ECE/external-clock2 despite exact TIM12 lacking them. RM1298/1303/1307/1322 mention center/down modes despite upcounter and CR1 reserved DIR/CMS. Do not import these family features.

RM1284 lists TIM3/4/5/16/17 trigger sources absent on C542; preserve raw table but exclude unavailable producers. Only ITR0/1/2/6/7/9 correspond to present TIM1TRGO/TRGO2,TIM2TRGO,TIM8TRGO/TRGO2,TIM15TRGO. Exact C542 HAL trigger-selection branch independently allows ITR0/1/2/6/7/9.
RM1309 says UEV generated if URS low; RM1286 and CR1 distinguish UEV/shadow transfer from interrupt suppression. Preserve conflicting summary rather than block all updates with URS1.
RM1298 general sentence says CNT<=CCR while detailed PWM1 same page and OCM1326 use CNT<CCR. Preserve inequality discrepancy.
RM1311 describes rising edge but programs CC2P1 (inverted/falling according to1328). Use field semantics; example not executable ground truth.
RM1329 ARR reset is0xFFFF; map1333 prints all zero. Map1332 PSC omits named field, whereas1329 describes PSC15:0. Preserve register-description/map inconsistencies.

RM1283 prints reversed reserved range15:18;1331 TI2SEL final code0100 labels input15 despite4-bit encoding. Same page CCR2 names nonexistent CCMR2 instead of CCMR1;1329 calls status TIM_ISR and diagram labels UIFCPY rw while prose says read-only. No extra field/register admitted.
DS87 external-clock ceiling kernel/2 conflicts with RM1282/1283 below kernel/4 input limit; no higher rate admitted.

DS21 prescaler1..65535 differs from DS20 and RM raw+1 through65536. DS21 general-purpose16/32bit up/down wording does not override exact upcount-only TIM12. DS87 footnote includes absent TIM5/16/17; no instance or channel capability inferred. DS20 table6 shows a merged Yes DMA-generation cell for general-purpose timers; No is in the complementary-output column. This differs from the exact TIM12 header exclusions and RM DIER/register map. Keep the discrepancy explicit; no TIM12 DMA admission.

RM1332 calls registers16-bit mapped while RM1314 explicitly permits16/32-bit writes and8/16/32-bit reads. RM1291 diagram labels TS00111 ETR while exact SMCR1319 reserves it. Use explicit access/selection restrictions, not generic drawing.
